blocks.text:
The test passes locally. The CI failure is a flake — but a systematic one. Let me understand the failure mode precisely by simulating the CI conditions.

The test: `ContendedClock` spikes 4 of 5 doubled runs with +30ms. minRatio over 3 attempts must be < 3.2. Failed with 3.2976...

Key insight: the min doubled time = the real (unjittered-or-not) time of the ONE clean doubled run per attempt. If the runner is slow such that the doubled run's real time is inflated relative to small runs' real time by >3.2x in all 3 attempts, the test fails.

Wait, but for the ratio to be 3.3 in ALL attempts... Let me think about the actual measured numbers in CI. On the CI runner with coverage, a 100k wrap might take ~10ms, and the doubled ~20ms (linear = 2x). For ratio 3.3: doubled min ≈ 33ms vs small ≈ 10ms. Hmm — 33ms is suspiciously close to the 30ms spike! 

WAIT. What if the spike itself is the min?! If the clean doubled run's real time (say 20ms under coverage on slow runner) is LESS than spiked runs (20+30=50ms), min = 20ms → ratio 2. Fine. But what if the small runs are FASTER than I assume...

Hmm, alternatively — what if the doubled real time exceeds 30ms+small-ish? No: min(doubled) = min(4 spiked, 1 clean). Spiked ≥ 30ms + real. Clean = real. So min = min(clean_real, spiked min). If clean_real < 30ms, min = clean_real.

Ratio = clean_real / small_min. For this to be 3.3 in the BEST attempt, the clean doubled run must measure 3.3x the small min. On a 2-core CI runner where the doubled wrap really takes 2x the small wrap, you need +65% inflation of the clean doubled run's measurement relative to small min in EVERY attempt.

Hmm, that's a lot of inflation for all 3 attempts... unless there's something systematically inflating the LAST doubled run (the clean one, always index 5 of the batch):

1. GC: the 200k-cell wrap allocates heavily; each spiked run allocates garbage too; the clean 5th run may hit major GC. But would that hit all 3 attempts? GC pressure is systematic: 4 spiked runs × big allocations → heap grows → next allocation-heavy run (the clean one) triggers GC. That's a SYSTEMATIC pattern, not luck!

Actually wait — but the small batches have the same structure (5 runs of 100k). Their min is over 5 clean runs, so one GC hit among 5 doesn't move the min. The doubled batch has only ONE clean run, and it's systematically the run right after 4 allocation-heavy runs. GC heuristics: after enough allocation, a major GC triggers. The clean run is plausibly the one that crosses the GC threshold EVERY attempt (deterministic-ish allocation pattern!). And in the small batch, the GC would hit one of the 5 runs — min unaffected.

Hmm interesting — but also the small batch runs right before the doubled batch, cleaning things. Let me think about the timeline per attempt:
- warm-up small (untimed), 5 timed small runs → allocations ~5×(100k tokens...). 
- warm-up doubled (untimed), 4 spiked + 1 clean doubled runs → allocations ~6×(200k).

Dart's GC is generational (new space scavenges + old space mark-sweep). 200k-cell string: the input string itself is 400KB (ASCII → 1 byte per code unit in Dart... actually Dart strings are one-byte for Latin1). Tokenization creates many small objects — mostly new-space → scavenges. A scavenge pause on ~200MB/s allocation rate... each wrap of 200k cells probably allocates a few MB (parts list, substrings? Actually the rewrite "batches same-width rune runs into single tokens (one substring + one carried width per run)" — one substring per token! For 200k cells at width 80 → 250 rows, words ~6 chars → ~33k words → ~33k substrings + parts list growth. Each wrap allocates maybe 2-5 MB new-space. New space is a few MB → scavenge every wrap or two.

A scavenge is typically fast (<1ms) but with a large live set can be slower. +65% on a 20ms run = +13ms — that's a LOT. Scavenges aren't usually 13ms... old-space GC could be.

2. Another systematic factor: JIT! In each attempt, `build(baseCells)` and `build(baseCells*2)` are called inside `expectLinearGrowth` — wait no, the builds are outside timing. The warm-up per minWrapMs handles JIT per size.

3. What about the `_rng` global state and `asciiProse(200)` — wait, baseCells=1000: `asciiProse(1000)` → the string is 100k chars. OK.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider — maybe the CI numbers are just what they are; I can't see the raw timings from the log (the failure message only prints the ratio). Let me check if the junit artifact has more detail... The workflow uploads junit. Let me look at the full log around the failing test for the printed reason — it only had the ratio.

OK let me think about what to do differently: instead of divining exact CI timing internals, design a fix that makes the deterministic-contention test robust to real jitter on the CLEAN run, without weakening the real growth assertions.

The purpose of this test (PR #1635 validation): prove `expectLinearGrowth` (min-based, cross-atempt min) survives sustained contention poisoning ≥3 of 5 doubled runs in EVERY attempt. The mechanism: each attempt has exactly one clean doubled run; the cross-atempt MIN rides it.

The fragility: that single clean doubled run per attempt carries the ENTIRE proof — real wall-clock jitter on it (GC, scheduler steal — the same phenomenon the test models!) inflates the minRatio. 3 attempts × 1 clean run = 3 real-timed samples; all 3 must be clean. On a contended runner, that's the SAME failure shape as the live reds: one slow sample among few.

Fix options:

A. Spike fewer doubled runs: 3 of 5 → 2 clean doubled runs per attempt → 6 real samples. Still models "contention poisons every attempt median" (median-of-5 with 3 spiked values = median is spiked — wait, median of 5 with 3 spiked: sorted [clean, clean, spiked, spiked, spiked] → median = spiked ✓. With 4 spiked: [c,s] → median = s ✓ too). Both shapes poison the median. Reducing to 3 spiked keeps the modeled shape EXACTLY ("a contention window spanning ≥3 of the 5 timed runs" — the live reds were ≥3!) and doubles the clean-run redundancy. This matches the live reds' modeled shape MORE faithfully than 4-of-5.

B. Make the injected spike scale relative to the measured clean time... no — ContendedClock is deterministic; complexity.

C. Increase attempts (3→5): more chances for one clean attempt. Weaker per-atempt shape.

D. Losen _maxLinearRatio: no — weakens the real guard.

E. Exclude the spike-induced floor differently: make the clean runs count by running the clean run FIRST (spike indices 6,7,8 vs 7,8,9)? No real difference.

F. Address GC: reduce allocation in measurement... no, out of scope.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the actual numbers once more. CI ratio 3.297687871853. If clean doubled real ≈ 2× small, ratio would be 2. 3.3 means inflation of the clean doubled sample by 65% relative to small min (if small is unjittered) — OR the small min was UNUSUALLY FAST. Hmm! Here's another angle: minWrapMs of the SMALL input takes the min of 5 clean real runs — that's fine, the min of noisy samples ≤ true value + noise. The min is biased DOWNWARD as an estimator... no, min ≥ true value in expectation... min over noisy samples approaches the true cost from above. Fine.

Let me look at actual CI timing: could the doubled wrap really be >3.2x the small wrap on 2 cores? NO — other tests in the same file with real timing passed: "growth ratio is pause-proof", "wrapped output stays contract-clean at scale" passed, and in OTHER shards the 500k growth tests passed (shard 0/1/3 green — but those don't run this file; the file is only in shard 2). Hmm wait, actually which shard runs this file? Shard 2 — it's the only shard that ran wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart. So I can't compare across shards.

But the FIRST growth tests in the file (real-timed, 500k cells): from the log, "✅ wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose..." — wait, were they in the passing list? The log showed "❌ ... survives contention that poisons every attempt median" and the "Passing tests" group listing several wrap_ansi tests. Let me pull the full log for this file to see all its tests' pass/fail status and any timing prints.

**Bug**: CI run 39546301132 went red (`Core tests (shard 2/4)` → `Quality gate` → `Advance vpinned marker`) on a single test failure: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" measured best doubling ratio 3.2977x against the 3.2x bound.

**Fix approach**: spike **3 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`{6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`) instead of 4 — the documented live-red shape. Failure now requires both clean samples contaminated in all 3 attempts. The 30-call layout guard is unchanged.

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1732 ([ci-red] v1.0.614 failed)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: CI run 39546301132 went red (`Core tests (shard 2/4)` → `Quality gate` → `Advance vpinned marker`) on a single test failure: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" measured best doubling ratio 3.2977x against the 3.2x bound.

**Root cause**: the deterministic contention-validation test itself has a single-sample fragility. `expectLinearGrowth` gates on the min ratio across 3 attempts; the test models "contention poisons every attempt median" by spiking **4 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}`), which leaves exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled run per attempt — 3 real samples total carry the whole assertion. Real scheduler/GC jitter on that one clean sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflates the attempt's min ratio: measured locally under load, one clean sample hit 11.587ms vs the ~7.3ms typical doubled time → attempt ratio 3.250. In CI (coverage instrumentation, shared 4-core runner, parallel test files) all 3 attempts' single clean samples were inflated → min ratio 3.2977 > 3.2 → red. The 4-of-5 spike shape is also stricter than the documented live reds it models ("a contention window spanning ≥3 of the 5 timed runs", PR #1635 reds fa runs 38824807299/38830911279).

**Evidence**: in the same shard, on the same runner, all three *real* growth tests (`wrap time grows linearly: ASCII/CJK/hard-cut, 500k cells`) passed — the wrap itself is linear; only the one-clean-sample deterministic shape red. Local probe (`dart test` on this commit, contended sandbox) reproduced a 3.250x attempt ratio from a single jittered clean sample while the cross-attempt min still passed (min of {1.809, 3.250, 2.122}).

**Impact**: flaky CI red; no product defect. `wrapAnsiLine` is linear; the failure is confined to the test harness's contention modeling. Each recurrence burns a full CI run, red-blocks the quality gate, and blocks the `vpinned` provenance marker from advancing.

**Fix approach**: spike **3 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`{6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`) instead of 4 — the documented live-red shape. Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value (sorted `[c,c,s]` → median = spiked), so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails (validation strength preserved). The min-based harness now has **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, so a single real-jittered clean sample no longer inflates the attempt min; the cross-attempt min rides the best attempt. Failure now requires both clean samples contaminated in all 3 attempts. The 30-call layout guard is unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — this is a fresh CI-red ticket (no prior dev PR for gh-1732). Prior hardening history of the same gate: gh-1532 introduced min-based statistics + cross-attempt min; PR #1635 added the deterministic sustained-contention validation test (this failure is its first live red, in the very shape it guards against).

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean
- Full CI shard-2 invocation (`dart test --coverage --exclude-tags integration` over `scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 2`) re-run locally — see notes

- The `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` job failures in run 39546301132 are downstream consequences of the shard failure ("fail on any real failure" / provenance gate requires green); they need no separate fix — the next green ref run closes them.
- Under harsher-than-CI synthetic saturation (5x oversubscription) the pre-existing absolute-budget test (`1M visible ASCII cells < 100ms`) can trip locally; it has generous headroom in the real CI environment (passed in the red run) and is intentionally left untouched — the growth-shape asserts remain the real regression guard.

blocks.text:
My local probe reproduces the flake shape RIGHT NOW on this machine: attempt 1 measured ratio 3.250 — the clean doubled run (call 20) took 11.587ms while the small min was 3.565ms. The clean doubled run is inflated 3.25x over small — REAL jitter (11.587 vs the ~7.3ms typical doubled time = +4.3ms of noise, i.e. a GC pause or scheduler steal on that one run).

So the structure: minRatio = min over attempts of (single clean doubled run / small min). With exactly ONE real-timed doubled sample per attempt, one +4ms GC pause on that sample pushes the attempt ratio from ~2.0 to ~3.25. In CI, all 3 attempts' clean samples were inflated (3.297 best) → red.

My local probe confirms the mechanism: the single clean doubled run per attempt is a single point of failure; a ~10% real pause relative to the spiked runs is enough. Local machine ALSO shows the clean-run contamination (call 20: 11.587ms vs typical 7.2-7.3ms).

Let me also check: could there be a systematic GC at the batch end? Attempt 1 calls 16-20: 21.0 (spiked, real 21?? wait no — call 16 printed 21.005ms TOTAL... no wait, the print shows t BEFORE adding spike? Let me re-read my probe: I print `t` (real time) and return t + spike. So call 16 real = 21.0ms?? That's inflated (spiked runs also get real pauses). Call 20 real = 11.587ms — the clean run, +4.3ms over typical. Attempt 2: call 26 real 9.3ms, call 28 real 16.9ms — even spiked runs show real jitter. So this sandbox is contended right now, and the clean run contamination happens frequently — attempt 1's clean run was inflated and the ratio hit 3.25 (just under 3.2? no, 3.250 > 3.2! If this were the actual test, attempt 1 ratio 3.25 — the test survived only because minRatio takes the min across attempts: min(1.809, 3.250, 2.122) = 1.809 < 3.2 ✓).

In CI all three attempts must have been ≥3.297. With contamination probability ~1/3 per clean sample (as observed locally), P(all 3 contaminated) ≈ 3% — rare but recurring on 4x-more-loaded CI runners with coverage. This matches: the flake has now red twice live (gh-1532 era reds were the MEDIAN harness), PR #1635 fixed median-poisoning, and this NEW deterministic validation test itself is fragile in exactly the same way it guards against — one clean sample per attempt, no redundancy.

The fix: give the min-based statistic more clean samples to ride on, while keeping the modeled contention shape faithful ("contention poisons every attempt median"). Two complementary changes:

1. Spike 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4 — median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still spiked ([c,c,s] median = s), so the modeled "contention poisons every attempt median" shape is preserved EXACTLY (the live reds spaned "≥3 of the 5 timed runs" — 3 is the documented minimum shape), and each attempt gets TWO clean doubled samples → the per-atempt min survives one contaminated clean sample. Contamination probability per sample locally ~1/3 → P(atempt ratio > 3.2) with 2 samples both contaminated ~1/9 → P(all 3 attempts) ~0.2%. Plus cross-atempt min on top: P(fail) ≈ (1/9)^3 ≈ 0.14%... hmm, with independence. Much better than (1/3)^3 = 3.7%.

Wait — should I keep 4-of-5 spikes and instead lower the spike margin? No — the spikes aren't the problem; the clean-sample redundancy is.

2. Also consider bumping `_growthAttempts` for this test... attempts are fixed inside expectLinearGrowth (_growthAttempts = 3 const). Changing the global const affects the real timing tests (makes them longer — CI time). Not needed if I fix the deterministic shape.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the design. The point of the deterministic test is: "if EVERY attempt's median is poisoned, the min-based cross-atempt statistic still passes". The essential property to validate: the min-based statistic ignores spiked measurements and rides clean ones. With 2 clean doubled runs per attempt, this property is still validated (median poisoned, min rides the clean pair). The stricter shape (exactly 1 clean) tested a property the real harness doesn't promise: robustness with only ONE clean sample — which we now know is inadequate in production too (the CI red proves the single-sample design fails when the clean sample itself gets contaminated).

Hmm — but hold on. Should I instead fix `expectLinearGrowth` itself (the product function used by the REAL tests)? The real CI red came from the deterministic test, but the same underlying fragility applies to the real 500k growth tests: their doubled sample is a min of 5 CLEAN runs — plenty of redundancy. The real tests are fine (min of 5 real runs; contamination needs 3+ of 5 contaminated, which is the sustained shape that red PR #1635 validation... wait, that's EXACTLY what happened in the gh-1532 era: sustained contention spanning ≥3 of 5 doubled runs inflated the per-atempt MIN too — no wait, with median it failed; the min harness (gh-1532) then red again when contention spaned 4+ of 5 runs in every attempt (PR #1635 reds: "best ratios 3.35x/3.31x at 500k cells"). Hmm! So the REAL harness (min of 5) failed live when ≥... let me re-read the sustained test comment:

"a contention window long enough to span ≥3 of the 5 timed runs of the doubled size in EVERY attempt inflates every attempt MEDIAN, so the cross-atempt min cannot rescue it."

Hmm — the gh-1532 harness was min-based already ("the min across attempts covers windows longer than one attempt"). The PR #1635 validation reds (runs 3824807299, 3830911279) had "best ratios 3.35x/3.31x at 500k cells" — the MIN-based real measurement failed! That means in those runs, ≥4 of 5 doubled runs were contaminated in EVERY attempt (min needs ≥4 of 5 contaminated to be inflated... actually the min is contaminated if ALL 5 are contaminated; if 4 of 5, min = the 1 clean → not contaminated. For the min-based ratio to hit 3.35, all 5 doubled runs per attempt must have been inflated, or 4 contaminated + the clean one partially inflated).

So PR #1635's fix for the REAL tests was... what exactly? The test file's comments say the PR added `minWrapMs` ("the fastest observed run is the least-contaminated estimate"). And the deterministic validation test I'm debugging was added to validate that harness against the sustained shape.

And NOW the deterministic validation test itself red in CI — with the same signature (3.297 vs 3.2) — because its clean doubled sample is singular (4-of-5 spiked leaves exactly 1 clean run; if that ONE clean run is real-contaminated, the attempt min is inflated; all 3 attempts → red).

So the correct root cause statement: the deterministic sustained-contention validation test leaves only ONE unspiked doubled run per attempt; the gate then rests on 3 real-timed samples total (one per attempt). Real scheduler/GC jitter on those samples — the very phenomenon the test models — inflates them (observed locally: attempt 1 clean sample +60% → ratio 3.25; CI: best ratio 3.297 > 3.2). The modeled shape is also stricter than the documented live reds ("≥3 of 5" — the test spikes 4 of 5).

Expected ratio: min over 2 clean samples ≈ 2x, plenty under 3.2. Update the spiked set + comment. Keep the layout guard (30 calls).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1732 ([ci-red] v1.0.614 failed)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: CI run 39546301132 went red (`Core tests (shard 2/4)` → `Quality gate` → `Advance vpinned marker`) on a single test failure: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" measured best doubling ratio 3.2977x against the 3.2x bound.

**Root cause**: the deterministic contention-validation test itself has a single-sample fragility. `expectLinearGrowth` gates on the min ratio across 3 attempts; the test models "contention poisons every attempt median" by spiking **4 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}`), which leaves exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled run per attempt — 3 real samples total carry the whole assertion. Real scheduler/GC jitter on that one clean sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflates the attempt's min ratio: measured locally under load, one clean sample hit 11.587ms vs the ~7.3ms typical doubled time → attempt ratio 3.250. In CI (coverage instrumentation, shared 4-core runner, parallel test files) all 3 attempts' single clean samples were inflated → min ratio 3.2977 > 3.2 → red. The 4-of-5 spike shape is also stricter than the documented live reds it models ("a contention window spanning ≥3 of the 5 timed runs", PR #1635 reds fa runs 38824807299/38830911279).

**Evidence**: in the same shard, on the same runner, all three *real* growth tests (`wrap time grows linearly: ASCII/CJK/hard-cut, 500k cells`) passed — the wrap itself is linear; only the one-clean-sample deterministic shape red. Local probe (`dart test` on this commit, contended sandbox) reproduced a 3.250x attempt ratio from a single jittered clean sample while the cross-attempt min still passed (min of {1.809, 3.250, 2.122}).

**Impact**: flaky CI red; no product defect. `wrapAnsiLine` is linear; the failure is confined to the test harness's contention modeling. Each recurrence burns a full CI run, red-blocks the quality gate, and blocks the `vpinned` provenance marker from advancing.

**Fix approach**: spike **3 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`{6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`) instead of 4 — the documented live-red shape. Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value (sorted `[c,c,s]` → median = spiked), so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails (validation strength preserved). The min-based harness now has **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, so a single real-jittered clean sample no longer inflates the attempt min; the cross-attempt min rides the best attempt. Failure now requires both clean samples contaminated in all 3 attempts. The 30-call layout guard is unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — this is a fresh CI-red ticket (no prior dev PR for gh-1732). Prior hardening history of the same gate: gh-1532 introduced min-based statistics + cross-attempt min; PR #1635 added the deterministic sustained-contention validation test (this failure is its first live red, in the very shape it guards against).

# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean
- Full CI shard-2 invocation (`dart test --coverage --exclude-tags integration` over `scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 2`) re-run locally — see notes

### Notes

- The `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` job failures in run 39546301132 are downstream consequences of the shard failure ("fail on any real failure" / provenance gate requires green); they need no separate fix — the next green ref run closes them.
- Under harsher-than-CI synthetic saturation (5x oversubscription) the pre-existing absolute-budget test (`1M visible ASCII cells < 100ms`) can trip locally; it has generous headroom in the real CI environment (passed in the red run) and is intentionally left untouched — the growth-shape asserts remain the real regression guard.

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1732 ([ci-red] v1.0.614 failed)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: CI run 39546301132 went red (`Core tests (shard 2/4)` → `Quality gate` → `Advance vpinned marker`) on a single test failure: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" measured best doubling ratio 3.2977x against the 3.2x bound.

**Root cause**: the deterministic contention-validation test itself has a single-sample fragility. `expectLinearGrowth` gates on the min ratio across 3 attempts; the test models "contention poisons every attempt median" by spiking **4 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}`), which leaves exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled run per attempt — 3 real samples total carry the whole assertion. Real scheduler/GC jitter on that one clean sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflates the attempt's min ratio: measured locally under load, one clean sample hit 11.587ms vs the ~7.3ms typical doubled time → attempt ratio 3.250. In CI (coverage instrumentation, shared 4-core runner, parallel test files) all 3 attempts' single clean samples were inflated → min ratio 3.2977 > 3.2 → red. The 4-of-5 spike shape is also stricter than the documented live reds it models ("a contention window spanning ≥3 of the 5 timed runs", PR #1635 reds fa runs 38824807299/38830911279).

**Evidence**: in the same shard, on the same runner, all three *real* growth tests (`wrap time grows linearly: ASCII/CJK/hard-cut, 500k cells`) passed — the wrap itself is linear; only the one-clean-sample deterministic shape red. Local probe (`dart test` on this commit, contended sandbox) reproduced a 3.250x attempt ratio from a single jittered clean sample while the cross-attempt min still passed (min of {1.809, 3.250, 2.122}).

**Impact**: flaky CI red; no product defect. `wrapAnsiLine` is linear; the failure is confined to the test harness's contention modeling. Each recurrence burns a full CI run, red-blocks the quality gate, and blocks the `vpinned` provenance marker from advancing.

**Fix approach**: spike **3 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`{6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`) instead of 4 — the documented live-red shape. Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value (sorted `[c,c,s]` → median = spiked), so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails (validation strength preserved). The min-based harness now has **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, so a single real-jittered clean sample no longer inflates the attempt min; the cross-attempt min rides the best attempt. Failure now requires both clean samples contaminated in all 3 attempts. The 30-call layout guard is unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — this is a fresh CI-red ticket (no prior dev PR for gh-1732). Prior hardening history of the same gate: gh-1532 introduced min-based statistics + cross-attempt min; PR #1635 added the deterministic sustained-contention validation test (this failure is its first live red, in the very shape it guards against).

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean
- Full CI shard-2 invocation (`dart test --coverage --exclude-tags integration` over `scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 2`) re-run locally — see notes

- The `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` job failures in run 39546301132 are downstream consequences of the shard failure ("fail on any real failure" / provenance gate requires green); they need no separate fix — the next green ref run closes them.
- Under harsher-than-CI synthetic saturation (5x oversubscription) the pre-existing absolute-budget test (`1M visible ASCII cells < 100ms`) can trip locally; it has generous headroom in the real CI environment (passed in the red run) and is intentionally left untouched — the growth-shape asserts remain the real regression guard.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1732 ([ci-red] v1.0.614 failed)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: CI run 39546301132 went red (`Core tests (shard 2/4)` → `Quality gate` → `Advance vpinned marker`) on a single test failure: `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" measured best doubling ratio 3.2977x against the 3.2x bound.

**Root cause**: the deterministic contention-validation test itself has a single-sample fragility. `expectLinearGrowth` gates on the min ratio across 3 attempts; the test models "contention poisons every attempt median" by spiking **4 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8,9, 16,17,18,19, 26,27,28,29}`), which leaves exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled run per attempt — 3 real samples total carry the whole assertion. Real scheduler/GC jitter on that one clean sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflates the attempt's min ratio: measured locally under load, one clean sample hit 11.587ms vs the ~7.3ms typical doubled time → attempt ratio 3.250. In CI (coverage instrumentation, shared 4-core runner, parallel test files) all 3 attempts' single clean samples were inflated → min ratio 3.2977 > 3.2 → red. The 4-of-5 spike shape is also stricter than the documented live reds it models ("a contention window spanning ≥3 of the 5 timed runs", PR #1635 reds fa runs 38824807299/38830911279).

**Evidence**: in the same shard, on the same runner, all three *real* growth tests (`wrap time grows linearly: ASCII/CJK/hard-cut, 500k cells`) passed — the wrap itself is linear; only the one-clean-sample deterministic shape red. Local probe (`dart test` on this commit, contended sandbox) reproduced a 3.250x attempt ratio from a single jittered clean sample while the cross-attempt min still passed (min of {1.809, 3.250, 2.122}).

**Impact**: flaky CI red; no product defect. `wrapAnsiLine` is linear; the failure is confined to the test harness's contention modeling. Each recurrence burns a full CI run, red-blocks the quality gate, and blocks the `vpinned` provenance marker from advancing.

**Fix approach**: spike **3 of the 5** doubled runs per attempt (`{6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`) instead of 4 — the documented live-red shape. Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value (sorted `[c,c,s]` → median = spiked), so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails (validation strength preserved). The min-based harness now has **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, so a single real-jittered clean sample no longer inflates the attempt min; the cross-attempt min rides the best attempt. Failure now requires both clean samples contaminated in all 3 attempts. The 30-call layout guard is unchanged.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — this is a fresh CI-red ticket (no prior dev PR for gh-1732). Prior hardening history of the same gate: gh-1532 introduced min-based statistics + cross-attempt min; PR #1635 added the deterministic sustained-contention validation test (this failure is its first live red, in the very shape it guards against).

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.
- feat(providers): gh-1704 — first-class Codex/ChatGPT credential export,
  CI refresh action, and Provider Queue integration (Copilot-export
  parity). `fa provider export <name> [--check]` resolves the saved
  ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot, refreshes it when
  stale, and prints the shell lines (`OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL`
  = the Codex backend — these tokens never serve api.openai.com); the
  refresh token never prints and `--check` reports credential health with
  the SSO caveat. `/provider chatgpt import [path]` adopts an existing
  `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`) into the same slot — no
  browser round-trip. `.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth` mints a fresh
  access token from a `CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` secret in CI (direct curl,
  no third-party action); invalid_grant fails fast and loudly.
  `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex`: an omitted `apiKeyEnv`
  resolves the Keychain slot automatically (in-memory refresh), a new
  `refreshTokenEnv:` field mints the initial access token on slot
  activation, and a raw Bearer token in `apiKeyEnv` is tolerated by
  `chatgpt_codex.dart` (no more FormatException — proactive/reactive
  refresh degrade, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over
  on).

blocks.text:
# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean
- Full CI shard-2 invocation (`dart test --coverage --exclude-tags integration` over `scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 2`) re-run locally — see notes

- The `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` job failures in run 39546301132 are downstream consequences of the shard failure ("fail on any real failure" / provenance gate requires green); they need no separate fix — the next green ref run closes them.
- Under harsher-than-CI synthetic saturation (5x oversubscription) the pre-existing absolute-budget test (`1M visible ASCII cells < 100ms`) can trip locally; it has generous headroom in the real CI environment (passed in the red run) and is intentionally left untouched — the growth-shape asserts remain the real regression guard.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.
- feat(providers): gh-1704 — first-class Codex/ChatGPT credential export,
  CI refresh action, and Provider Queue integration (Copilot-export
  parity). `fa provider export <name> [--check]` resolves the saved
  ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot, refreshes it when
  stale, and prints the shell lines (`OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL`
  = the Codex backend — these tokens never serve api.openai.com); the
  refresh token never prints and `--check` reports credential health with
  the SSO caveat. `/provider chatgpt import [path]` adopts an existing
  `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`) into the same slot — no
  browser round-trip. `.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth` mints a fresh
  access token from a `CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` secret in CI (direct curl,
  no third-party action); invalid_grant fails fast and loudly.
  `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex`: an omitted `apiKeyEnv`
  resolves the Keychain slot automatically (in-memory refresh), a new
  `refreshTokenEnv:` field mints the initial access token on slot
  activation, and a raw Bearer token in `apiKeyEnv` is tolerated by
  `chatgpt_codex.dart` (no more FormatException — proactive/reactive
  refresh degrade, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over
  on).

  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner
  jitter only ever inflates a wall-clock sample, so the min converges on
  the true compute time; genuine superlinearity still trips the ratio
  (the gh-1496 quadratic candidates measure ~4x by min). The absolute-
  budget legs keep the median — their gh-1357 headroom already prices in
  jitter. A synthetic regression test pins the pause-proof property.

publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated

publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean
- Full CI shard-2 invocation (`dart test --coverage --exclude-tags integration` over `scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 2`) re-run locally — see notes

### Notes

- The `Quality gate` and `Advance vpinned marker` job failures in run 39546301132 are downstream consequences of the shard failure ("fail on any real failure" / provenance gate requires green); they need no separate fix — the next green ref run closes them.
- Under harsher-than-CI synthetic saturation (5x oversubscription) the pre-existing absolute-budget test (`1M visible ASCII cells < 100ms`) can trip locally; it has generous headroom in the real CI environment (passed in the red run) and is intentionally left untouched — the growth-shape asserts remain the real regression guard.

`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.
- feat(providers): gh-1704 — first-class Codex/ChatGPT credential export,
  CI refresh action, and Provider Queue integration (Copilot-export
  parity). `fa provider export <name> [--check]` resolves the saved
  ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot, refreshes it when
  stale, and prints the shell lines (`OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL`

{"content":"### Root Cause

CI run 39546301132 red on a single test: `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` "growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median (PR #1635 validation red ×2)" — best doubling ratio 3.2977x vs the 3.2x bound. The deterministic contention test spikes 4 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt, leaving exactly **one** real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt; real scheduler/GC jitter on that single sample (the very phenomenon the test models) inflated all 3 attempts' min ratios. In the same shard the three real 500k growth tests stayed green — `wrapAnsiLine` itself is linear; the gate's sample redundancy was the defect.

### Previous Attempt

PR #1635 added this deterministic validation test proving the min-based growth harness survives sustained contention. Its 4-of-5 spike shape was stricter than the documented live reds it models ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs") and left no redundancy on the clean sample.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart`: sustained-contention shape changed from 4-of-5 to 3-of-5 spiked doubled runs per attempt (`spiked: {6,7,8, 16,17,18, 26,27,28}`). Median-of-5 with 3 spiked values is still a spiked value, so the test still proves the pre-gh-1532 median harness fails; the min-based harness now rides **two** clean doubled samples per attempt, tolerating one contaminated clean sample. Comment documents the gh-1732 live red (run 39546301132). No product code touched.

### Test Coverage

- `growth assertion survives contention that poisons every attempt median` — PASSED (5/5 standalone runs; also green under 2x and 5x synthetic CPU oversubscription, which red the old shape locally at 3.25x)
- Static gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.
- feat(providers): gh-1704 — first-class Codex/ChatGPT credential export,
  CI refresh action, and Provider Queue integration (Copilot-export
  parity). `fa provider export <name> [--check]` resolves the saved
  ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot, refreshes it when
  stale, and prints the shell lines (`OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL`
  = the Codex backend — these tokens never serve api.openai.com); the
  refresh token never prints and `--check` reports credential health with
  the SSO caveat. `/provider chatgpt import [path]` adopts an existing
  `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`) into the same slot — no
  browser round-trip. `.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth` mints a fresh
  access token from a `CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` secret in CI (direct curl,
  no third-party action); invalid_grant fails fast and loudly.
  `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex`: an omitted `apiKeyEnv`
  resolves the Keychain slot automatically (in-memory refresh), a new
  `refreshTokenEnv:` field mints the initial access token on slot
  activation, and a raw Bearer token in `apiKeyEnv` is tolerated by
  `chatgpt_codex.dart` (no more FormatException — proactive/reactive
  refresh degrade, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over
  on).

  legs measure the doubling ratio with the MINIMUM over 9 runs instead of
  the median of 5 (CI run 38112524699, core shard 0/4: a scheduling pause
  inflated the doubled-size median — 12.09ms against a true ~7ms — and
  tripped the 3.2 bound at 3.65x on a genuinely linear wrap). Runner
  jitter only ever inflates a wall-clock sample, so the min converges on
  the true compute time; genuine superlinearity still trips the ratio
  (the gh-1496 quadratic candidates measure ~4x by min). The absolute-
  budget legs keep the median — their gh-1357 headroom already prices in
  jitter. A synthetic regression test pins the pause-proof property.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
  and only `Custom` continues into the api-type wizard; a preset opens its
  own flow with the api type prefilled. Previously boarding opened the
  custom wizard directly, cold-asking "api type" before any provider was
  chosen.

  CI refresh action, and Provider Queue integration (Copilot-export

  ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot, refreshes it when

  = the Codex backend — these tokens never serve api.openai.com); the
  refresh token never prints and `--check` reports credential health with

  `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`) into the same slot — no
  browser round-trip. `.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth` mints a fresh
  access token from a `CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` secret in CI (direct curl,
  no third-party action); invalid_grant fails fast and loudly.
  `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex`: an omitted `apiKeyEnv`
  resolves the Keychain slot automatically (in-memory refresh), a new
  `refreshTokenEnv:` field mints the initial access token on slot
  activation, and a raw Bearer token in `apiKeyEnv` is tolerated by

  refresh degrade, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over
  on).
